rfi.title: Migration to wealthy countries slows for second year amid tougher rules
rfi.description: Legal migration to developed countries dropped for a second year in a row in 2025, down 1.6 percent compared to the previous year, as governments tightened rules for workers, students and refugees, according to an OECD report published Thursday. But the figures show sharply diverging trends – with big increases in Southern Europe and sharp declines in North America.

rfi.title: Medical charity warns funding for DRC Ebola fight not reaching front lines
rfi.description: Six months into the Democratic Republic of Congo's Ebola outbreak, the virus is continuing to spread and international aid is not reaching the front line, French medical charity Doctors Without Borders said on ‌Thursday.

rfi.title: African push to triple climate adaptation finance left off Cop31 agenda
rfi.description: African countries’ proposal to triple finance for adaptation to the effects of climate change has been left off the agenda at the United Nations climate summit Cop31, currently under way in Antalya, Turkey. Wealthy nations pushed back against efforts to make it a formal, binding agenda item.

rfi.title: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom as first black senator since 19th century
rfi.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith on Wednesday in Mississippi's closely contested United States Senate race, after a prolonged ballot counting process – giving the state its first black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction period.

rfi.title: DR Congo leader opens way for third term under new constitution

rfi.title: Zidane confirms Mbappe to miss France's Nations League game against Italy
rfi.description: France's captain Kylian Mbappe will miss his country's Nations League match against Italy due to a hamstring injury, coach Zinedine Zidane said on Wednesday.

rfi.title: France's Macron to pay state visit to Cambodia during Francophonie summit
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte will make a state visit to Cambodia from 14 to 16 November at the invitation of King Norodom Sihamoni. During the visit, Macron will attend the 20th Francophonie Summit, which Cambodia is hosting in Phnom Penh on 15 and 16 November. It will be the first visit by a French president to Cambodia since Charles de Gaulle’s in 1966.

rfi.title: UN chief urges world leaders to tackle 'dinosaur' fossil fuels at Cop31
rfi.description: United Nations secretary-general Antonio Guterres railed against the oil and gas lobby on Wednesday, telling world leaders fossil fuels "must go the way of the dinosaurs" at a climate summit that is missing several prominent figures.

rfi.title: France requests arrest warrants for Iranian suspects over supermarket cyberattack

rfi.title: Teachers divided over compulsory 11 November ceremonies at schools
rfi.description: A new government initiative requires primary schools across France to hold ceremonies honouring those who died for the country. But teachers are divided over its purpose and the role of the military in education.

rfi.title: Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race vowing to expel unemployed foreigners
rfi.description: Far-right politician Eric Zemmour has formally entered next year’s French presidential race. He is promising a sharp cut in immigration, and the expulsion of foreigners who are out of work, even if they live in France legally.

rfi.title: As Senegal sets Youth Games medal record, Olympic hero calls for more investment
rfi.description: With wins in taekwondo, beach wrestling, judo and three-a-side basketball, hosts Senegal have clocked up a record nine medals at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar – starting from a previous tally of zero. But if the country wants to replicate this success in the future, investment and infrastructure are key, according to its sole adult Olympic medal winner.

rfi.title: Cameroon sets February date for long-delayed parliamentary and local elections

rfi.title: Macron rallies world leaders behind charter to protect children from AI risks
rfi.description: The annual Paris Peace Forum has placed artificial intelligence among the key topics on its agenda. rfi.title: France threatens consequences for Iran after linking it to supermarket cyberattacks

Les hommes de Sebastien Desabre sont quasiment qualifiés pour la prochaine Coupe d'Afrique qui aura lieu au Kenya, en Tanzanie et en Ouganda.

france24fr.title: Candidature de Teddy Riner, primaire de la droite et du centre
france24fr.description: Le judoka Teddy Riner est candidat à la présidentielle. Emmanuel Macron s'est réjoui de cette annonce. L'objectif est maintenant de transformer sa popularité en voix. L'arrivée du sportif dans la course à l'Elysée, peut-elle affaiblir d'autres candidats ? Pendant ce temps, les discussions se poursuivent autour d'une primaire du centre et de la droite. Edouard Philippe s'y oppose mais la pression de ses concurrents s'accentue. Le candidat Horizons pourra t-il échapper à cette primaire ?

france24fr.title: Israël interdit l'entrée sur son territoire à Jean-Luc Mélenchon
france24fr.description: Le leader de LFI et candidat à l'élection présidentielle en France, Jean-Luc Mélenchon, a reçu l'interdiction d'entrer en Israël, a fait savoir le ministère israélien des Affaires étrangères, accusant La France insoumise de tenir une "position extrêmement hostile à Israël".

france24fr.title: COP31: Le Népal, martyr du climat, en quête de réparations
france24fr.description: Le Népal a subit 2 catastrophes climatiques juste avant la COP31 qui ont fait des milliers de morts et de disparus. Pour la première fois, le fond pertes et dommages a promis une aide d'urgence mais elle tarde à être versée et ne couvrirait qu'une infime part des besoins de reconstruction. Le sentiment d'injustice est grand pour le Népal qui ne représente que 0,1% des émissions mondiales de gaz à effet de serre mais est l'un des pays les plus exposé aux catastrophes climatiques.

france24fr.title: Un Congolais "chef de village" au Canada ? Une rumeur alimentée par de faux contenus de France 24
france24fr.description: La rumeur circule en ligne depuis début novembre : un Congolais installé au Canada se serait autoproclamé chef de village et aurait imposé sa loi pour vendre des terrains. L'histoire, inventée de toutes pièces, repose sur de faux contenus usurpant l'identité de France 24.

france24fr.title: Rugby : les Bleus amoindris affrontent le rouleau compresseur sud-africain
france24fr.description: Le XV de France a un défi de taille à relever, vendredi, au Stade de France face aux maîtres du rugby mondial, les Springboks sud-africains. Ces joueurs adeptes d'un jeu très physique vont s'appuyer sur leur puissance pour tenter de battre des Bleus décimé par les blessures, au sein desquels le capitaine Antoine Dupont évoluera à un poste inhabituel.

france24fr.title: CAN 2027 : au pied du mur, le Ghana fait le travail face à la Somalie
france24fr.description: Alors que les Black Stars n'ont déjà plus leur destin en mains dans les éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, ils ont lancé avec succès leur opération sauvetage. Lors de la troisième journée, le Ghana s'est imposé à domicile 2 à 0 face à la Somalie et guette maintenant le résultat de la rencontre Côte d'Ivoire – Gambie.

france24fr.title: COP31 : l'Union européenne se désengage-t-elle de la diplomatie climatique ?
france24fr.description: Seuls cinq dirigeants sur les 27 de l'Union européenne ont fait le déplacement à Antalya pour le sommet des leaders de la COP31. Le Commissaire européen au Climat, Wopke Hoekstra, a estimé qu'il y avait "peu d'attentes" pour cette COP. Au moment où le monde s'apprête à dépasser 1,5°C de réchauffement climatique, l'Union européenne, jusque-là leader des négociations climatiques, semble se mettre en retrait. Cela pourrait compliquer l'adoption d'un communiqué ambitieux.

france24fr.title: Ces images relayées par Israël prouvent-elles vraiment que la nourriture est abondante à Gaza ?
france24fr.description: Début novembre, les autorités israéliennes ont diffusé plusieurs vidéos censées montrer que de la nourriture est présente en grandes quantités dans la bande de Gaza. Mais selon les ONG, ces images sont loin d’être représentatives de la réalité, même si la situation s’est améliorée depuis le cessez-le-feu du 10 octobre 2025.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : Donald Trump retire le dossier de la guerre en Iran à JD Vance
france24fr.description: Le président américain a affirmé jeudi 12 novembre ne pas "avoir besoin d'un accord avec l'Iran". Dans le même message, Donald Trump dit avoir demandé à son vice-président JD Vance de concentrer ses efforts sur "la corruption et le crime massifs" dans les États et villes gérés par les démocrates, qu'il qualifie de "désastres corrompus". Les précisions de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Une fusillade dans une salle de sport à Washington fait au moins un mort
france24fr.description: Un homme a tiré sur la foule, jeudi, dans une salle de sport près de la Maison Blanche à Washington, avant de se suicider. Au moins une personne est morte et quatre ont été blessées.

france24fr.title: Sommet en Irlande : les Européens se réunissent à Dublin
france24fr.description: Pendant deux jours à partir de ce jeudi 12 novembre, Dublin sera un lieu de rencontre pour les dirigeants européens. Près de 50 chefs d'État ou de gouvernement européens se retrouvent au Convention Centre afin d'échanger sur des sujets cruciaux : le coût de l’énergie, la sécurité européenne, la place de l’IA dans les entreprises ou encore la guerre en Ukraine.

france24fr.title: Australie : un adolescent retrouvé vivant après six jours passés dans le bush
france24fr.description: Voici le moment où un adolescent porté disparu a été retrouvé vivant, après avoir survécu six jours seul dans le bush australien. William, 17 ans, dont le nom de famille n’a pas été communiqué, avait disparu le 6 novembre alors qu’il campait avec un ami, à environ 180 km à l’est de Melbourne.

france24fr.title: Afghanistan : des oliviers pour lutter contre la sécheresse
france24fr.description: Dans un pays où le manque d'eau affecte plus de la moitié de la population, selon l'ONU, les 500 villageois de Saïdan Arabi cherchent des alternatives à la culture du maïs, du riz ou du blé, comme celle de l'olive. Si elle n'est pas traditionnelle, la production d'huile d'olive n'est cependant pas tout à fait nouvelle en Afghanistan : des deux côtés de la route reliant la frontière avec le Pakistan et Jalalabad, surgit d'immenses oliveraies évoquant l'Espagne ou l'Italie.

france24fr.title: Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse : dernière ligne droite
france24fr.description: Un dernier effort avant la clôture. Les Sénégalais diront aurevoir ce vendredi aux Jeux olympiques de la Jeunesse. Le pays a vibré au rythme du futsal, de la lutte de plage, de l'escrime. Retour sur cette épopée avec Sarah Sakho, à Dakar.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : huit morts dans l'effondrement d'un immeuble à New York
france24fr.description: Le nombre de victimes de l'effondrement d'un immeuble survenu à New York s'est considérablement alourdi jeudi 12 novembre au matin avec huit morts et 19 blessés, dont quatre dans un état critique. Les 250 secouristes ont passé la nuit à fouiller le site où l'immeuble s'est effondré à Flatbush, quartier populaire de Brooklyn.

france24fr.title: France : le pays devient-il le nouvel eldorado des data centers ?
france24fr.description: En France, 68 projets de data centers sont en cours selon les observatoires spécialisés, bien qu'un collectif d'opposant en ait décompté 110. Ces énormes centres de données utilisés surtout pour l'intelligence artificielle, sont déjà plus de 300 en France et leur présence suscite de plus en plus d'opposition, à cause du bruit et l'impact sur l'écologie.

zeit.title: GTA VI: Weltweit mehr Urlaubsanträge zum Start von Grand Theft Auto VI
zeit.description: Der Start von dem Videospiel GTA VI könnte in der kommenden Woche für ungewohnt leere Büros sorgen. Beschäftigte weltweit haben dafür Urlaub beantragt.

zeit.title: Bundeshaushalt: CDU-Vorschlag zu Stromsteuersenkung sorgt für Streit mit CSU
zeit.description: Mathias Middelberg hält eine Stromsteuersenkung für wichtiger als eine Ausweitung der Mütterrente. Damit geht der CDU-Politiker auf Konfrontationskurs zur CSU.

zeit.title: Nico Rosberg: »In vielen Fällen blitze ich eiskalt ab«
zeit.description: Formel-1-Weltmeister Nico Rosberg trat auf dem Höhepunkt ab. Jahrelang suchte er ein neues Ziel. Und merkte dann, dass er ohne den Druck zu siegen nicht leben kann.

zeit.title: Trumps Zolldrohung: Mexiko soll Flüchtlingsstrom stoppen
zeit.description: Eine Gruppe von mehreren hundert Menschen, geschätzt rund 1500 und überwiegend aus Mittelamerika stammend, bricht am Dienstag in der südmexikanischen Stadt Tapachula nahe der Grenze zu

zeit.title: Antisemitismus: Gießener Synagoge wegen verdächtigen Briefs evakuiert
zeit.description: Nach dem Fund eines antisemitischen Drohbriefs in der Gießener Synagoge wurden umliegende Teile der Innenstadt geräumt. Die Feuerwehr prüft den Brief auf Gefahrstoffe.

zeit.title: Rettungskräfte im Einsatz: Landeskriminalamt übernimmt Ermittlungen zu Synagoge
Spionageaffäre: Jensen Huang soll vor US-Kongress zu Spionageaffäre aussagen
zeit.description: US-Abgeordnete pochen auf eine Befragung von Jensen Huang auch nach dessen Rücktritt. Notfalls werde der Ex-Nvidia-Chef eine Vorladung erhalten.

zeit.title: Tierseuche: Geflügelpest trifft Betrieb mit 39.000 Legehennen
Kapitalmärkte: EU-Parlament stimmt gegen neue Schutzregeln für Kleinanleger
Bundestag: Bundestag gibt Sicherheitsbehörden neue Cyberabwehr-Befugnisse
zeit.description: Sicherheitsbehörden sollen sich künftig aktiv gegen Hackerangriffe wehren können. Ein entsprechendes Gesetz passierte den Bundestag. Die Opposition warnt vor den Folgen.

zeit.title: Kriminalität: Zehn Tote im vergangenen Jahr durch häusliche Gewalt
Leitindex: Optimismus an der Börse - Dax erstmals über 27.000 Punkten
Koalition in Berlin: Scheitert eine rot-grün-rote Koalition an dieser Frau?
zeit.description: Ein Linksbündnis in Berlin wäre eine Grenzüberschreitung, sagt der Grüne Danyal Bayaz aus Baden-Württemberg. Sein Parteifreund Daniel Eliasson widerspricht.

zeit.title: Regierungsbildung im Nordosten: Linke stimmt auf Parteitag über Koalitionsvertrag in MV ab
Nvidia-Affäre: Bei aller Liebe
zeit.description: Jensen Huang tritt wegen einer Affäre zurück. Das deutsche Start-up Helsing entwickelt KI-Kriegsgerät. Und: Anthropic veröffentlicht Fable 5.2. Der KI-Newsletter

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Es ist höchste Zeit für einen Kurswechsel in der deutschen Finanzpolitik
nzz.description: Die Regierung verweigert sich dem nötigen Sparkurs im Bundeshaushalt. Das lässt die Staatsschulden weiter rasant steigen und setzt die Europäische Zentralbank unter Druck. Deutschland und Europa droht eine finanzielle Repression.

nzz.title: Scott Colom schreibt Geschichte: Nach 152 Jahren schickt Mississippi wieder einen schwarzen Senator nach Washington
nzz.description: Im konservativen Gliedstaat schien ein Erfolg der Demokraten undenkbar. Doch Colom hat seine Kontrahentin nach allen Regeln der Kunst ausmanövriert. Damit macht er den Erdrutschsieg seiner Partei bei den Zwischenwahlen perfekt.

nzz.title: Der Fall Embolo beschäftigt das Schweizer Nationalteam weiter. Und Manuel Akanji wird zum Vermittler
nzz.description: Xhaka fehlt, Manzambi reist ab – das Schweizer Nationalteam gastiert in Slowenien ohne seine besten Fussballer. Aber das Sportliche gerät ohnehin einmal mehr in den Hintergrund.

nzz.title: VIDEO - Jugendlicher überlebt sechs Tage alleine im australischen Outback
nzz.description: Ein Jugendlicher verschwand in Australien bei einem Campingausflug – fast eine Woche später fanden ihn Einsatzkräfte in Cowwarr lebend. Abgesehen von Sonnenbrand und ein paar Kratzern überstand der junge Mann die Tage in der Wildnis unbeschadet.

nzz.title: Droht ein Schweizer Shutdown? Eine unheilige Allianz im Nationalrat stellt sich gegen das Budget 2027 des Bundesrates
nzz.description: Die Finanzkommission beschliesst Mehrausgaben von 241 Millionen Franken. Trotzdem lehnt eine Mehrheit den Budgetvorschlag des Bundesrates ab. In der Wintersession steht eine hitzige Debatte bevor.

nzz.title: Colette Kress übernimmt als Nvidia-Chefin: Warum der Verwaltungsrat so lange brauchte, um Jensen Huang zu entlassen
nzz.description: Der Nvidia-Verwaltungsrat ist schlecht aufgestellt und handelt erst in der Not. Die Governance-Mängel beim wichtigsten Tech-Unternehmen der Welt sind akut. Daran ändert auch der Rücktritt von Jensen Huang nichts.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Gewalt und Waffen in den USA: Ein Toter und mehrere Verletzte nach Schüssen in Washington
nzz.description: In keinem anderen Land sind Schusswaffen und die damit verübten Massaker so verbreitet wie in den USA. Warum ist das so? Dies sind die Nachrichten sowie die wichtigsten Zahlen und Fakten zur amerikanischen Schusswaffengewalt.

nzz.title: Felix Nmecha bringt mit seinem Torjubel die Dortmunder Fans in Rage. Nun reagieren der Verein und der DFB
nzz.description: Die Anhänger des BVB fordern Vielfalt ein. Aber sie haben selbst Mühe, diesem Anspruch gerecht zu werden.

nzz.title: Ist das nicht cool? Die Schweiz hat mit ihren Sprachregionen ein Herz und mehrere Seelen
nzz.description: Zürich und die Waadt wollen den Sprachaustausch von Jugendlichen weiter fördern. Das täte dem ganzen Land gut: Die Schweiz könnte so ihren grössten Vorteil nutzen. Essay eines Bilingue.

nzz.title: Radikale Pläne für preisgünstige Wohnungen – Kritiker befürchten Entstehen von DDR-Plattenbauten
nzz.description: Zug will als erster Kanton in gewissen Zonen die Bauvorschriften ausser Kraft setzen. So sollen beispielsweise 100-Meter-Hochhäuser problemlos möglich sein.

nzz.title: Es begann mit einem «Bünzli»-Streit um ein Ikea-Produkt. Und endet nun damit, dass der Kanton Zürich tatsächlich die Bauvorschriften vereinfacht
nzz.description: Ein Strauss von FDP-Vorstössen zeigt Wirkung: So sind etwa für Pergolen und Rutschen im Garten künftig keine Baubewilligungen mehr nötig.

nzz.title: MELDUNGEN ZÜRICH - Trinkwasser in Zürcher Gemeinde verunreinigt – Einwohner sollen Wasser abkochen
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Krieg in der Ukraine: Grossbritanniens Premier Andy Burnham kündigt neue Sanktionen gegen Russland an
nzz.description: Seit über vier Jahren führt Russland Krieg gegen die Ukraine. Die wichtigsten Entwicklungen im Überblick.

nzz.title: «Roboter statt Einwanderer»: Nun tritt auch Éric Zemmour bei der französischen Präsidentschaftswahl an – mit einem eigenwilligen Programm
nzz.description: Der rechtsidentitäre Publizist scheiterte 2022 bei seinem Versuch, den Élysée-Palast zu erobern. Jetzt will er es erneut versuchen. Für die Kandidatin des Rassemblement national Marine Le Pen könnte das nützlich sein.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Die Karikatur der Woche
nzz.description: Der Karikaturist Peter Gut kommentiert in seinen wöchentlichen Zeichnungen für die NZZ das Weltgeschehen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Ebola-Ausbruch in Zentralafrika: Infizierte Schweizerin in Genf laut Angaben des Spitals entlassen
nzz.description: Die Weltgesundheitsorganisation (WHO) hat den Gesundheitsnotstand ausgerufen. Die Infektionszahlen steigen weiterhin an. Die wichtigsten Antworten zum Ebola-Virus.

observador.title: CEO da Nvidia caiu "no truque mais antigo do mundo"
observador.description: A demissão do CEO da Nvidia foi tema de última hora de um painel da Web Summit. Se há quem considere "um erro", também há quem defenda que "é o fim da ideia mitológica do fundador genial".

observador.title: As notícias das 18h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Sánchez: a estratégia do abraço de urso à esquerda
observador.description: O Partido Popular e o Vox somam uma maioria clara nas intenções de voto. Para travar a maioria da direita, o líder do PSOE tenta absorver o eleitorado da esquerda radical.

observador.title: Putin mantém-se inflexível com exigências para fim à guerra
observador.description: Mais de duas horas de negociações não abalaram as exigências russas. Witkoff e Kushner seguem para Dublin, onde Zelensky fala em "janela de oportunidade" antes de 2027.

observador.title: "Pedro Tinto": nova queixa do Chega contra deputado do PS
observador.description: José Carlos Barbosa acumula três queixas na Comissão de Transparência nesta legislatura. O socialista ironiza e pede desculpas "à Associação das Tascas Portuguesas".

observador.title: MP abre investigação a intervenção policial em Lisboa
observador.description: A Procuradoria-Geral da República anunciou que o MP abriu inquérito para investigar a intervenção policial nas manifestações pela habitação, que resultou na detenção de vários manifestantes em Lisboa.

observador.title: GNR deteve 16 suspeitos de crimes ambientais com lamas
observador.description: Investigação culminou no cumprimento de 36 mandados de busca, dos quais 15 domiciliários, 13 em instalações de empresas de gestão e valorização de resíduos e oito em instalações de entidades pública.

observador.title: Cristina Ferreira "contrata" Daniela Braga para lançar app
observador.description: A apresentadora e administradora da TVI encerrou a Web Summit em Lisboa. Chamou ao palco Daniela Braga, CEO da DefinedAI, para anunciar o lançamento de uma nova plataforma.

observador.title: Google quer manter anulação de multa de 1,5 mil milhões
observador.description: A advogada-geral Juliane Kokott recomendou ao Tribunal de Justiça da UE que reverta a anulação da coima imposta à Google pelo serviço de publicidade AdSense. A empresa rejeita a posição.

observador.title: PCP exige fiscalização da ACT após depressão Charles
observador.description: Paula Santos enviou pergunta à ministra do Trabalho e pede que faltas sejam justificadas e dias pagos. "Os trabalhadores não podem perder o dia", afirmou.

observador.title: Impostos com relevância ambiental nos seis mil milhões
observador.description: O crescimento de 1,6% da receita ambiental, impulsionado pelo ISP, ficou abaixo dos 6,8% do total fiscal, fazendo cair o peso destes impostos no PIB para 1,9%.

observador.title: A IA não perdoa a traição: ataca o ex-CEO e defende a esposa
observador.description: Os problemas dos romances do fundador da Nvidia com a espia chinesa e com a vice. O governo aprendeu com a Kristin, mas a tendência para fechar sempre vai trazer problemas. E ainda o ciclone de 1941.

observador.title: Tenho mais de 60, não me chamo Tom Cruise. Uso cabedal?
observador.description: Pode parecer uma frivolidade mas a dúvida existencial varreu a internet e reabriu um velho debate sobre possíveis crises de meia idade -- ou se é boa ideia usar roupa arriscada quando se pisa o risco.

observador.title: Harriet Philips: elogios à princesa Ana e conselhos de Kate
observador.description: 5 meses depois de se casar com Peter Phillips, deixa o trabalho de enfermeira para ser patrona numa instituição. Elogia a princesa Ana, o Rei e a Rainha, e elege Kate como conselheira.

observador.title: Cambra desiste de providência cautelar contra Moedas
observador.description: Abandono voluntário da Praça do Rossio por parte da acampada leva manifestante a desistir da providência cautelar contra decisão de Carlos Moedas sobre o Mercado de Natal.

observador.title: PS acusa Governo de "conflitualidade" em vez de dialogar
observador.description: Brilhante Dias rejeitou críticas do ministro das Finanças à garantia pública para senhorios e avisou que o PS fiscalizará o Governo em 2027 sobre os apoios às zonas afetadas pelas tempestades.

observador.title: Fiasco. Rimac Nevera foi descontinuado antes de atingir 50%
observador.description: O Rimac Nevera continua a ser um dos melhores superdesportivos eléctricos do mercado. Com potências de até 2107 cv e um máximo de 430 km/h, o Nevera é brutal — até no fiasco.

observador.title: 17h. Montenegro reage a declarações de Mark Rutte
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro considera que o secretário geral da NATO mostrou-se "infeliz, ligeiro e desconhecedor". Ainda, José Luís Carneiro, considera que Portugal deve repensar os investimentos em Defesa.

letemps.description:
Les juges de Strasbourg reprochent aux autorités helvétiques l’usage excessif de la force lors d’une arrestation en 2018 et l’insuffisance des investigations menées. La Confédération doit verser près de 10 000 francs

Ayant provoqué des polémiques dans plusieurs pays, le groupe de hip-hop nord-irlandais Kneecap s'est produit au Festi'Neuch et il est programmé à Lausanne et Genpve. A Zurich, les partis bourgeois veulent empêcher son arrivée. A Bâle, c'est une cantatrice pro-Poutine qui fait débat

letemps.description:
Fragilisé par deux affaires de relation extraconjugale, le cofondateur du géant américain des semi-conducteurs a démissionné. letemps.description:

letemps.description:
La «coalition contre l’austérité», qui regroupe syndicats, partis de gauche et une vingtaine d’associations, rêve d’une manifestation d’envergure samedi. Guillaume Thion, membre du SSP, appelle le Conseil d’Etat à revoir son plan d’économies

letemps.title: L’immigration vers l’OCDE recule mais les immigrés assurent la moitié de la croissance de l’emploi dans de nombreux pays

phys-org.description: The recent discovery of a Roman timber fort in the Preseli hills of Pembrokeshire, southwest Wales, has brought a medieval Welsh legend into fresh focus.

phys-org.title: A living shield: Skin microbes may help sawfish survive oxygen-poor pools
phys-org.description: This large freshwater sawfish might look scary, but its greatest survival assets are tiny microbes that may give its young an invisible force field when environmental conditions get tough. New research led by Flinders University describes how microscopic communities living on the skin of the critically endangered largetooth sawfish (Pristis pristis) could help these animals endure challenging dry-season conditions, offering a new perspective on their conservation.

phys-org.title: Lemon waste yields bioplastic more flexible than commercial counterpart, study finds
phys-org.description: A new research article published in Polymers explores an innovative way to turn lemon processing residues into biopolymers. Authored by ANIPH's coordinator, CETEC, together with partners from companion projects Viss and PHAntastic, the study investigated the use of lemon industry byproducts as carbon sources for PHBV production using the halophilic archaeon Haloferax mediterranei.

phys-org.title: Liquid-phase growth strategy densifies ceramic films at low temperature
phys-org.description: Ceramic films are widely used in solid-state batteries, energy conversion devices and electronic systems. Their fabrication, however, often requires high-temperature sintering, which can cause elemental volatilization, compositional segregation and undesirable interfacial reactions. Achieving dense, compositionally uniform ceramic films at lower temperatures therefore remains a challenge.

phys-org.description: The universe is filled with light at many different energies. Some of it is invisible to our eyes, including extremely energetic gamma rays, which can only be produced in the most extreme environments in our universe, for example supermassive black holes, exploding stars or astrophysical jets. phys-org.title: A suspected black hole turns out to be a rapidly spinning star

Such is the case with a strange pair of stars in the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) cluster NGC 1850. The system was initially thought to contain a star about five times the mass of the sun orbiting a stellar-mass black hole. phys-org.title: Pumpkin seed protein puts a twist on nondairy coffee creamer
phys-org.description: Pumpkin season is about more than cute décor. The squash contains lots of seeds with a high protein content, but they're usually discarded. Researchers reporting in ACS' Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry found another way to use the seeds, extracting that protein to create a plant-based coffee creamer. In initial taste tests, participants preferred the new creamer to a commercial nondairy option because it preserved the flavor and aroma of coffee better.

phys-org.title: Simulated collisions reveal how Phobos could preserve rocks blasted off Mars
phys-org.description: Mars has two small moons, Phobos and Deimos, but their origins remain uncertain. Were they asteroids captured by Mars' gravity, or did they form from debris following a giant impact on the planet?

phys-org.title: Sequential peaks in arthropod availability across snow and vegetation help sustain alpine birds
phys-org.description: The alpine zone is located above the tree line in mountainous regions and is characterized by long winters and short growing seasons. Birds and other animals inhabiting these environments breed during a limited period extending from spring to summer. Arthropods, including insects and spiders, serve as an essential food resource during this time.

phys-org.title: Finding romance with AI: Study explores benefits, limits of chatbot intimacy
phys-org.description: An AI companion can be available for a late-night conversation, respond to personal disclosures and discuss a favorite topic for hours. For people who develop intimate relationships with chatbots, those exchanges can offer a meaningful sense of connection.

phys-org.title: Lipids from banana peels help cherry tomatoes stay fresh longer
phys-org.description: Fruits and vegetables keep "breathing" even after they're picked. Respiration consumes sugars and organic acids that contribute to flavor, while moisture loss and continued ripening soften the fruit. These changes shorten shelf life and contribute to food waste. Thin edible coatings can be applied to regulate gas and water transfer and preserve fresh produce. Now, food scientists are exploring whether byproducts we often discard could supply ingredients for these coatings.

phys-org.description: As superbugs become harder to treat and antibiotic resistance continues to rise worldwide, Flinders University scientists have uncovered an unlikely ally in the fight to prevent infections before they take hold. They have found that carefully controlled microscopic cracks can enhance the performance of an antibacterial coating, which helps destroy dangerous bacteria when activated with a small electrical charge.

phys-org.title: Feeling pressured to be grateful? Don't force it

The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors

They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

undark.title: Book Review: An Optimistic Defense of Uncertainty in Science
undark.description: At an uncertain moment in the sciences, Stuart Firestein argues in favor of optimism in “It Could Be Otherwise,” since uncertainty leaves room for possibility, and possibility drives curiosity, imagination, and the agency to study the peculiarities of the natural world.

For Philip Sidney, they were simply indispensable. Florence Hazrat introduces us to the uncontested early modern king of brackets and to his romance Arcadia, which abruptly ends, like its author’s life, hanging on a parenthesis.

proj-syn.title: The Digital-Currency Divide
proj-syn.description: The rush to develop central bank digital currencies has slowed as underwhelming demand and mounting costs have given governments second thoughts. proj-syn.title: The ASEAN Paradox
proj-syn.description: As the Association of Southeast Asian Nations gathers for its 49th Summit, several rifts have exposed the group’s institutional shortcomings. But amid a fracturing global order, ASEAN must choose: turn its convening authority into concerted action or be reduced to an arena for great-power rivalry.

proj-syn.title: Medical AI Needs Bedside Manners
proj-syn.description: Even the most accurate medical AI tools have little value if they make patients uneasy or doctors find them too cumbersome. A comfort-by-design approach could overcome these obstacles by involving patients and practitioners in development and ensuring that new systems work with existing medical practices.

proj-syn.title: Reviving the Legacy of Reykjavík
proj-syn.description: As nuclear threats grow, AI accelerates, and international law comes under strain, the world urgently needs a renewed commitment to dialogue. Today's leaders can find a template in the landmark 1986 summit between then US President Ronald Reagan and Soviet President Mikhail Gorbachev.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s AI Dreams Exceed Its Grid
proj-syn.description: Europe is racing to expand its AI data-center capacity, but its power grids are already strained, and local communities are increasingly pushing back against new construction. Achieving technological sovereignty will require less grandstanding and more practical solutions that make better use of existing resources.

proj-syn.title: What the US Midterms Could Mean for AI
proj-syn.description: Now that the Democrats will hold sizable majorities in both chambers of the US Congress, they have an opening to push for long-overdue legislation to steer AI development toward the common good. Private companies should not have the power to decide unilaterally which risks the public will bear.

proj-syn.title: Let’s Publish AI-Generated Articles!
proj-syn.description: Peer-reviewed academic journals exist to advance our knowledge and understanding by publishing the best work being done in a given field. If that is the goal, and the best reviewers—both human and AI—agree that an article generated by AI meets that standard, why should a journal's editors reject it?

proj-syn.title: The AI Industry Should Make Something People Want
proj-syn.description: AI companies have alienated Americans by forcing them to bear the costs of their products while treating their consent as optional. With voters across the United States rejecting data centers, the incoming Congress has an opportunity to enact meaningful regulation and hold the industry accountable.

proj-syn.title: It’s the Corruption, Stupid
proj-syn.description: Fed up with Donald Trump and his family's blatant profiteering, Americans dealt Republicans a resounding defeat in this month’s midterm elections. Democrats won by linking corruption to the cost-of-living crisis, but the party’s establishment remains compromised and must clean house before 2028.

proj-syn.title: AI Investors Have Overlooked Obvious Risks
proj-syn.description: Prior to the US midterm elections on November 3, financial markets had been treating generative AI as some kind of unstoppable force that could not be hampered by higher interest rates or political and social resistance. But now reality may be setting in.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasure of Privacy
proj-syn.description: Over the past few decades, we have adopted a new framework for thinking about privacy that centers our experience in the digital realm, conflates privacy with secrecy, and fails to account for the insecurity surveillance generates. As a result, even privacy advocates often undermine their own cause.

proj-syn.title: The Right Lessons From Brazil and the US
proj-syn.description: One lesson progressives in both countries cannot afford to ignore is that recent election results do not amount to a mandate. Neither the Democrats in the US nor President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s Workers' Party in Brazil are offering a vision voters can get excited about.

proj-syn.title: A Russian Bribe the Size of Europe
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump is willing to sacrifice Ukraine in exchange for lucrative oil and gas deals with Russia, but this bargain is bound to backfire spectacularly. Vladimir Putin has a long record of betraying his business partners, and once he gets what he wants from Trump, Europe will be his next target.

proj-syn.title: Will Anthropic’s IPO Lead to Better AI Regulation?
proj-syn.description: When frontier AI labs go public, ordinary people’s investments and pensions become tied to their valuations and stock prices. While excessive regulation could undermine a firm’s growth, catastrophic accidents caused by inadequate safety measures could do the same—and wipe out shareholder value.

proj-syn.title: A Minimum Basic Income Is Not Enough
proj-syn.description: The rise of AI is concentrating wealth and political power in fewer and fewer hands, making extreme inequality a threat to democracy itself. A universal basic share that gives ordinary people a portion of global profits could help narrow the growing gap between billionaires and everyone else.

proj-syn.title: Scott Bessent’s Risky Short-Termism
proj-syn.description: The US Treasury secretary's commitment to accelerate buybacks of longer-term debt and issue more short-term debt in their place promises significant budgetary savings. But if borrowing costs rise, what happens in the T-bill market won’t stay in the T-bill market.

proj-syn.title: Why Trump Crowned the Man Who Cost Him Congress
proj-syn.description: By appointing Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff, US President Donald Trump has revealed what he cannot give up after decisive midterm losses. The moral depravity of one of the most widely reviled members of his administration is the citadel he will defend until the end.

proj-syn.title: Why Politicians Love Stimulus Checks
proj-syn.description: Stimulus checks sent to households promise to supercharge the economy, but much of the money simply sits in people's bank accounts. They are popular with voters but do little to address the underlying causes of economic downturns and leave future generations to foot the bill.

crunchbase.title: How Founders Can Reduce Platform Risk Before It Threatens Growth
crunchbase.description: Founders should treat dependence on app stores as infrastructure risk, since a sudden removal can disrupt customer access, subscriptions and revenue with no reliable path to reinstatement. Sharing his experience, Yakov Filippenko, founder and CEO of Intch, suggests that building and testing alternative access and payment channels before a crisis can help keep the business operating.

crunchbase.title: VCs Are Still Chasing Protein, Even As Fake Meat Falls Out Of Favor
crunchbase.description: Recent startup investment has shifted away from meat substitutes and toward stuffing more protein into other packaged foods and drinks. It’s a fad that’s obvious on supermarket shelves, where startups and established brands alike relentlessly tout the added protein in their noodles, pancakes, cereals, energy bars, popcorn and so on. We take a look.

crunchbase.title: Anthropic Seeks Record $88.5B Tied To Public Market Debut
crunchbase.description: Anthropic is seeking to secure up to $88.5 billion in its planned IPO and a concurrent private placement, potentially making it the largest-ever fundraise tied to a public market debut. On Tuesday, the AI giant submitted an updated S-1 filing for its upcoming public offering, unveiling new details including a proposed share price range offering size.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Unicorn Board Tops 1,900 Companies In October, With 34 Companies Joining — Half Under 4 Years Old
crunchbase.description: A total of 34 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in October, adding more than $96 billion in value and $14.8 billion in total funding to the board. The board also reached a new record of 1,900 private companies last month, along with a new record for the U.S. with more than 1,000 private unicorn companies.

crunchbase.title: Startup Founders Are Using AI To File Patents. Here’s Where DIY Becomes A Liability.
crunchbase.description: AI can help startups reduce patent preparation costs, but DIY applications may overlook critical issues. In this guest commentary, attorneys Michael Drapkin and Nathan Mutter of AI-Native law firm Landfall IP, argue that combining AI with legal expertise can produce more efficient, commercially valuable patent protection that withstands investor scrutiny and is harder for competitors to circumvent.

crunchbase.title: Series A In 2026: Capital Is Flowing Faster, But Fewer Startups Are Making The Cut
crunchbase.description: More money is pouring into Series A rounds, but it isn’t opening the door to more startups. U.S. companies have raised $42 billion at that stage this year through October, up roughly 60% year over year, while deal counts remain on pace with the past few years, Crunchbase data shows.

crunchbase.title: Paper Unicorns Are Cheap. Building A $1B Revenue AI Company Takes A Multimarket Cap Table
crunchbase.description: AI startups should be judged by durable revenue, full-price renewals and healthy margins after delivery costs, with embedded customer workflows providing stronger defensibility as model access gets cheaper, rather than their paper valuation, writes guest author Ilman Shazhaev, founder and CEO of Dizzaract, who suggests that founders should build global investor bases that support customer acquisition and market entry while weighing venture growth expectations against sovereign-backed investors’

crunchbase.title: The Week’s 10 Biggest Funding Rounds: AI, Defense And Space Tech Lead For Large Rounds
crunchbase.description: This week brought another plethora of large funding rounds for startups and growth-stage companies. Shield AI, a defense tech player focused on autonomy and virtual simulations, secured the largest financing, bringing in $2 billion. Next on the list was drone delivery provider Zipline International, which pulled in a fresh $1.5 billion.

crunchbase.title: How To Challenge A Monopoly In The AI Age
crunchbase.description: AI chip startups can challenge the sector's Goliath's by building substantially better hardware for emerging inference demands, much as Juniper challenged Cisco with a new architecture suited to the internet’s rapid growth. To win customers, writes guest author R K Anand, co-founder and chief product officer of Tensordyne, challengers must prove their advantages, make switching easy and use small, agile teams to anticipate needs that incumbents have yet to address.
